title: Vaidya Nath Vishwakarma v. State of U.P.
coram: Tarun Agarwala, J.; Vipin Sinha, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; pay earlier revised-bill arrears before fresh Clause 6.5 consideration.
headnote: A consumer whose earlier Clause 6.5 objection has already been decided and a revised bill issued must first clear those arrears before a later Clause 6.5 application will be considered afresh. The writ seeking a direction to decide a subsequent representation against a higher bill was disposed of on that condition.
facts: The petitioner had earlier obtained a writ direction dated 2 December 2014 in Writ-C No. 64856 of 2014 to file a Clause 6.5 objection for correction of his electricity bill. The Electricity Department decided that objection and issued a revised bill dated 7 January 2015, reducing the demand from Rs. 57,142 to Rs. 56,814, which the petitioner did not pay. He then filed this writ seeking a direction to decide a later Clause 6.5 representation dated 18 April 2016 against a bill of Rs. 1,21,235.

holding_units.holding: Where an earlier objection under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 has been decided and a revised bill issued, the consumer must first clear those arrears before a subsequent Clause 6.5 application on a later bill will be considered afresh.

not_decided.point: Merits of the 18 April 2016 Clause 6.5 representation and the bill of Rs. 1,21,235
not_decided.note: Left for consideration afresh under Clause 6.5 only after the 7 January 2015 revised-bill arrears are cleared.
